A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REArtGS, with matching main sections, equations, tables and figure content. All 11 pages of v3 and 12 pages of v4 were inspected. However, both end with references and omit the supplementary material or appendices they cite, limiting assessment of appendix-dependent changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction and generation experiments on PartNet-Mobility and AKB-48, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1, 2 and 5 and ablations in Tables 3 and 4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original quantitative experiments, ablations and qualitative reconstruction and generation results.

M1.justification: The core architecture, losses and deformation equations match. Section 3.2 newly describes heuristic joint-type prediction from point movement and sequential learning of individual parts' masks and motions. The missing appendix prevents reliably distinguishing procedural additions from newly disclosed implementation details.

E1.justification: The displayed experiments retain the same PartNet-Mobility and AKB-48 categories and reconstruction/generation tasks. Figure 6 also retains its examples despite newly mentioning multipart objects. However, v4 references segmentation and joint-parameter evaluations whose absent results leave any expansion of evaluated tasks unverified.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 includes A-SDF, Ditto, PARIS, GOF and ArtGS; Table 2 includes A-SDF, PARIS, D-3DGS and ArtGS; Table 5 includes PARIS and ArtGS. Newly cited ArticulatedGS is not included in a reported comparison.

E3.justification: The reported ray-sampled and whole-surface evaluations, CD scaling by 1000, F1 threshold of 0.4 and ArtGS control without depth supervision are retained. v4 omits view-count/sampling details and replaces explicit Chamfer-L1 wording with generic CD; these reduce specification without establishing an actual protocol change.

E4.justification: The SDF/unbiased-regularization ablation in Table 3 and motion-constraint ablation in Table 4 retain identical settings and results. v4 additionally points to segmentation and joint-parameter evaluations, but their missing destinations prevent checking whether supplementary component analyses were added.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained mean columns summarize categories rather than newly reported uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 match, and the displayed qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, mean reconstruction and generation CD(ws) remain 3.79 and 4.10. However, the segmentation and joint-estimation results newly referenced in v4 are unavailable, preventing comparison of those claimed additions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, motion assumptions and Equations (1)–(17) are unchanged. Neither supplied PDF includes the referenced proof. The expanded discussion of SDF linearity provides conceptual motivation rather than a new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion retain the same central claims: textured reconstruction and unseen-state generation from two states' RGB views using SDF geometric guidance and kinematic motion constraints, with superior synthetic and real-world performance.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explanation contrasting SDF and opacity-field linearity and explicitly discusses multipart applicability. The results discussion shifts emphasis toward ArtGS and removes discussion of categories favoring Ditto or PARIS and of D-3DGS failure mechanisms. Camera-pose dependence and transparent-material limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 removes the stated 64–100 and 100 training-view counts, upper-hemisphere training-view sampling, explicit Chamfer-L1 specification and Figure 6's ReArtVal provenance statement. It adds brief joint-type and multipart implementation descriptions, but directs details to an absent appendix. The project link remains, while the promised post-acceptance code release is no longer stated.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds ArticulatedGS and explicitly positions REArtGS against it and ArtGS on geometric constraints. CenterSnap and Shapo citations are removed, and the A-SDF/AKB-Net background is shortened. ArtGS was already cited and evaluated in v3.

P1.justification: The introduction's method motivation is expanded, while related work and experimental discussion are shortened or rewritten. Author-role information and acknowledgements are added, and supplementary-material references become appendix references. The section sequence and most method prose remain intact; Section 4.3 introduces an unresolved '??' reference.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a predominantly single-column NeurIPS layout, extensively resizing and relocating the same six figures and five tables. Tables 3 and 4 are placed side by side, Table 5 receives surrounding text, and captions are revised. In v4, Figure 3's caption overlaps Equation (2), impairing readability.

improvement.justification: v4 expands motivation and updates research positioning, but replaces useful experimental details with pointers to an absent appendix. It also introduces an unresolved reference and a Figure 3 caption overlap with Equation (2). With the displayed experimental evidence unchanged, these concrete losses of reproducibility and readability outweigh the modest explanatory gains.
